failure_summary.description: Calls included redundant validators or unrequested providers, or selected an endpoint returning categories instead of matching products.
Parameters were omitted, duplicated, placed in the wrong required/optional bucket, or added despite not being in the endpoint schema.
Location, market, or locale constraints were missed, scoped incorrectly, or sent using an unsupported or noncanonical value.

patch.reasoning: The batch shows repeated failures to turn existing broad guidance into hard checks. These edits make source scope and nonredundancy explicit, reinforce schema-based bucket validation, distinguish product discovery from category lookup, and clarify how to map geographic constraints without guessing.

edits.target: - Build the smallest complete call set: cover every requested outcome, and make every call serve one of them. Use one endpoint for multiple outcomes only when it genuinely covers them; make separate calls for distinct inputs unless the schema supports batching. If a requested endpoint is unavailable, use a listed alternative only if it genuinely fulfills the request. Do not invent tools, add unrelated calls, or include redundant alternatives or validators.
edits.content: - Build the smallest complete call set: cover every requested outcome, and make every call serve one of them. Treat explicitly named providers or platforms in a comparison as the requested source scope; do not add unnamed providers merely because the task asks for a comparison. Choose one endpoint for each distinct requested result property, and do not add another call when its result would repeat a property already covered. A request to use multiple tools means complementary checks for distinct requested properties, not every plausible validator. Use one endpoint for multiple outcomes only when it genuinely covers them; make separate calls for distinct inputs unless the schema supports batching. If an endpoint is unavailable, use a listed alternative only if it genuinely fulfills the request. Do not invent tools, add unrelated calls, or include redundant alternatives or validators.

edits.target: - For each selected endpoint, use only its own schema for exact parameter names, declared types, and required/optional placement; never borrow fields from similar operations. For parameters you include, put every required field in the required bucket and every non-required field in the optional bucket, even when the user explicitly requests an optional setting; never duplicate a field. In formats that represent parameters as name/value entries, every entry must have the exact name and a concrete non-null value—never emit name-only entries or null placeholders. Bind required values to the request or a documented derivation; if a required value is missing, do not call that endpoint rather than fabricate it. Treat documented finite choices as API-native values even if typed STRING, and use documented canonical codes and casing; preserve identifiers and free-text wording except where the endpoint specifies normalization. Include optional settings only when requested or clearly implied; use documented freshness controls for “recent” or “latest” and a modest supported result count for “some” or an open-ended list request (such as top headlines), when a count or limit field is available and the endpoint is not fixed-size. Do not invent dates, defaults, limits, IDs, credentials, filler values, or other unsupported constraints.
edits.content: - For each selected endpoint, first make a schema-only checklist of exact parameter names, types, and required/optional status. Put every supplied required parameter only in the required bucket and every selected non-required parameter only in the optional bucket; never duplicate a parameter or borrow fields from another endpoint. Before output, verify each name and bucket against that checklist. In name/value formats, every entry must have the exact name and a concrete value, with no name-only or null placeholders. Bind required values to the request or a documented derivation; if a required value is missing, do not call that endpoint. Use documented canonical codes, casing, and finite choices; preserve identifiers and free text except where the endpoint specifies normalization. Include optional settings only when requested or clearly implied. Do not invent dates, defaults, limits, IDs, credentials, empty-string fillers, or other unsupported constraints.

edits.target: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap.
edits.content: - Match the requested entity level and property as well as the topic: a result about a related component or sub-entity does not fulfill a request about the main entity, even when the search terms overlap. Match the returned content type too: product discovery requires an endpoint that searches or suggests matching products; a category or taxonomy listing does not show whether matching products are carried.

edits.target: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields, using accepted representations for enums and locales.
edits.content: - Preserve requested search text, identifiers, and constraints; normalize only as the endpoint requires, without dropping meaningful words or substituting one value or geographic level for another. Map explicit filters, counts, pages, sorting, locale, category, and location to the corresponding schema fields using accepted representations. For geographic and market fields, use the documented country, region, postal-code, or internal-ID form and canonical value; carry the location only to outcomes it qualifies. Do not substitute an arbitrary default market or guess an undocumented ID or code; if a required value cannot be derived from the request or documented schema, do not call that endpoint.
